issues.failure_explanation: The definition admits every real p >= 1, but for non-integer p the function h(eta) = eta^p/(eta^p + tau^p) ~ (eta/tau)^p near eta = 0 is not smooth there: for p = 3/2, h''(eta) ~ eta^{-1/2} diverges, so h is not even C^2 at 0. issues.title: Shut-off function claimed C-infinity on [0,1] for every real p >= 1
issues.why_classification: A local restriction of the admitted parameter set; every substantive claim, rate, and experiment survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement covers the general weights of Section 3, in which a cell of M_j may receive from other neighborhoods (W_i containing k != j) and neighborhood j's aggregate may feed cells outside M_j. The proof handles only 'the one-neighborhood case W_i = {j}', where w_{i,j} = 1 and S_j is plain volume-weighted merging. With cross-neighborhood coupling, cell values in M_j are pulled toward other aggregates scaled by s_j, while buffer cells that pure SRD would feed are frozen at U^*_i by the global operator ('identity on all other cells'), so the claimed balance sum_{i in M_j} V_i U_i^{n+1} = sum_{i in M_j} V_i U_i^* fails for 0 < s_j < 1. The stated per-cell constraint sum_j w_{i,j} = 1 alone does not imply conservation; the needed hypothesis (self-contained neighborhoods, or a common blending value across coupled neighborhoods) is never stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Each time step of UM-SRD can be decomposed into:

issues.failure_explanation: The proof chains Propositions TVD-SRD, TVD-Q-update and TVD-R for the staging pre-merge -> finite-volume update on the MERGED mesh -> blended redistribution. But the method defined in Section 3 and realized by Algorithm 1 has no pre-merge stage: the base upwind update runs on the ORIGINAL cut-cell mesh (so the small cell steps at local CFL nu/alpha, a non-monotone, TV-increasing step whenever nu > alpha), and only then is the SRD operator blended in (exactly the one-step form U^{n+1,UM} = (1-s)U^{n+1,base} + s S_j(U^{n+1,base}) used in the accuracy analysis). For that defined scheme TVD fails under the theorem's stated CFL a dt/h <= 1: take h = 1, alpha = 0.05, a dt/h = 0.5, data (U_{j-2}, U_{j-1}, U_j, U_{j+1}) = (0, 1, 0, 0), so TV(U^n) = 2. The base step gives U*_{j-1} = 0.5, U*_j = 10; then eta ~ 1, s = 1/1.01, Qhat* = (0.5 + 0.05*10)/1.05 = 1/1.05, and the update gives U^{n+1}_{j-1} ~ 0.948, U^{n+1}_j ~ 1.042, whence TV(U^{n+1}) ~ 0.948 + 0.094 + 1.042 = 2.18 > 2: total variation increases and a new maximum is created. The proof therefore establishes TVD for a different operator than the stated one.

issues.failure_explanation: (h V_{j-1} + alpha h V_j)/(h + alpha h) equals (V_{j-1} + alpha V_j)/(1 + alpha), a convex combination with weights 1/(1+alpha) and alpha/(1+alpha), not (1-alpha, alpha); the two agree only for alpha in {0,1}. The same wrong weights appear in Proposition srd-steady's displayed equation and inside its proof, and in Corollary steady-accumulation's formulas. The paper's own Experiment 6 evaluates the correct expression and obtains 5/3 = 1.6-with-bar, contradicting the proposition's stated value (which for alpha = 0.2, U_{j-1} = 1.5, U_j = 2.5 would be 1.7).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (1-alpha, alpha) by (1/(1+alpha), alpha/(1+alpha)) in the proof of Proposition local-consistency, in the displayed equation and proof of Proposition srd-steady, and in Corollary steady-accumulation; all orders, arguments, and Experiment 6's numbers then hold.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit post-redistribution values in Proposition srd-steady and the error formulas in Corollary steady-accumulation are false as written; the qualitative conclusions (standard SRD alters steady states; the perturbation (S_j - I)B(u^n) is O(h)) survive with the corrected constant alpha/(1+alpha).
issues.title: Volume-weighted neighborhood average mis-simplified: weights are 1/(1+alpha), not (1-alpha, alpha)
issues.why_classification: A local algebraic correction with changed constants; no inference, rate, or guarantee has to be restructured, and the corrected values match the paper's own numerics.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Then $s_j^n$ is not $\mathcal{O}(h^p)$ in smooth regions with nonzero updates; instead,
$s_j^n \approx 1/(1+\tau^p)$ whenever any update is present.

This means the normalized implementation does not satisfy the theoretical
scaling $s_j^n = \mathcal{O}(h^p)$ in smooth regions with nonzero updates.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary proves only the undivided one-step bound tau^UM - tau^base = s_j^n (S_j - I)B(u^n) = O(1) x O(h) = O(h). Under the paper's convention (tau = B(u^n) - u^{n+1}, one step, dt = Theta(h)), the base first-order scheme's LTE is O(h^2), so an O(h) perturbation is one order LARGER than the base LTE, not 'the same order'; an O(h) LTE supports only zeroth-order consistency, from which first-order global accuracy does not follow (the standard LTE-to-error argument would give an O(1) contribution). The inference 'same order as the base scheme, hence still first-order accurate' is therefore invalid; the conclusion may still be true (the O(h) defect acts at a fixed cell pair and equilibrates under advection), but that argument is absent. Additionally, the conclusion section asserts the normalized-indicator choice 'satisfies this scaling for any p >= 1', directly contradicting Section 4.7 ('does not satisfy the theoretical scaling'), and the abstract's unconditional 'local truncation error modification is higher-order' claim holds only for the unnormalized indicator with p >= 2, not for the implemented method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the corollary to consistency (the LTE perturbation is O(h), vanishing as h -> 0) with first-order convergence supported only empirically, or add a contained new argument (e.g., a modified-equation/defect-accumulation analysis showing the fixed-location O(h) defect equilibrates to an O(h) global error); the abstract and conclusion must stop claiming a higher-order LTE modification for the normalized indicator.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Using the full-mesh timestep violates the
small-cell CFL condition and causes the base scheme to diverge.
Under this timestep, the base upwind scheme diverges rapidly: $\max|U^n|$

issues.failure_explanation: The setup claims a dt/h <= 1 ensures stability of the base (redistribution-free) scheme. The base scheme runs on the original cut-cell mesh, where the small cell requires a dt/(alpha h) <= 1; a dt/h <= 1 does not provide this, and the paper's own Experiment 5 demonstrates the base scheme diverging at a dt/h = 0.5 <= 1 with alpha = 0.05. Hence the stated three-way comparison (base vs SRD vs UM-SRD) in Experiment 1 is not realizable under the timestep as described, and the timestep actually used is not stated.

failure_location.quote: The time step is chosen to satisfy the CFL condition $a \Delta t / h \le 1$, ensuring stability of the base scheme on the merged mesh.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the timestep actually used (e.g., one respecting a dt/(alpha h) <= 1, under which all three schemes are stable); all reported numbers can stand under the clarified configuration.
issues.overall_effect: The experimental configuration as described is internally inconsistent (its stability claim is refuted by Experiment 5), leaving the reported three-method error comparison of Experiment 1 without a specified, stable configuration.
issues.title: Experimental setup claims the full-mesh CFL ensures base-scheme stability, contradicted by Experiment 5
issues.why_classification: A one-line clarification of the experimental timestep preserves every reported number and conclusion.
